messages:
Aisha: Heads-up — proposal to switch console telemetry storage from wide event blobs to a sparse metrics model. Need a quick sync on migration path (dual-write, backfill, read-adapter) and rough rollout plan.

Aisha: TL;DR: dual-write for ~2 weeks, read adapter for compatibility, incremental backfill (low-cardinality first), canary on staging, cutover per-route-group.

Tom: LGTM in general. Main worry is dashboard query perf — many dashboards do joins over envelope fields. Can we keep materialized aggs for the high-traffic ones?

Nina: +1 on materialized aggs. Also the quota computation depends on envelope shape today. We need a compatibility shim that returns the same billing fields during dual-write.

Jorge: How big is the backfill if we try to do a full historical copy? That will spike IO/ingest. Suggest per-tenant, windowed backfill with throttling and prioritization.

Priya: Agree with Jorge. We should implement an incremental backfill job that's idempotent and resumable. Example compact schema sketch:
```sql
CREATE TABLE compact_metrics (
  tenant_id text,
  metric_key text,
  bucket_ts timestamptz, -- minute-bucketed
  value double precision,
  tags jsonb,
  last_seen timestamptz,
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, metric_key, bucket_ts)
);
```
This keeps queries simple and avoids full denormalization.

Aisha: Important: SDK and the internal telemetry client must emit both shapes during dual-write. That means an SDK bump + feature flag. Ops teams can enable per-service.

Tom: Rollout proposal: 1) SDK + client bump (opt-in), 2) enable dual-write on a small canary fleet, 3) run read-adapter in front of dashboards for ~2w, 4) backfill low-cardinality metrics, 5) evaluate query perf and unit cost, 6) cutover with feature-flag switch.

Nina: For rollback, we should have auto-fallback in the read-adapter: if compact read p50 > 150ms or error rate > 2% then route to the legacy read path.

Aisha: Agreed — read_routing should implement that policy and expose metrics so we can alert.

infra-bot: perf-test job queued: metrics-backfill-sim on jiggy-cluster (job id 4872).

Jorge: One more thing — tag cardinality. Store high-cardinality tags in the event blob (as a pointer) and avoid indexing them in compact store. That'll keep compact table small.

Priya: Also recommend minute-bucketing (as in schema) + quantized sampling for very high-frequency metrics to cut storage by ~4x. We'll measure accuracy impact.

Tom: And telemetry retention/costs need to be reconciled. Update billing join keys so usage reports match during migration. Otherwise finance dashboards will be noisy.

Aisha: Action items: Nina to draft read-adapter PR and compatibility tests, Priya + infra to prototype backfill with throttling/resume, Tom to own rollout checklist and canary plan. I'll schedule a sync Thu 10am. :calendar:

Nina: I'll start a PR draft today and include a fallback mode.

Priya: Prototype ETA EOD Wed for backfill runner.

Jorge: I'll work with infra to estimate IO surface for prioritized tenants.

Tom: I'll sketch the canary runbook and dashboards to watch (latency, error-rate, cost-per-token). :thumbsup:

Aisha: Thanks all — keeping this thread for updates. If we hit perf regressions we'll pause auto-cutover and revert routing.
